title: Congratulate a specific effort
description: Congratulate someone for a specific effort, not a vague trait.
oneStarDescription: Say the specific effort they made, in a sentence they would recognize.
twoStarDescription: Add why that effort mattered to the work or the people there.
threeStarDescription: Leave out a label about the kind of person they are, and send or say the note.

title: Convert 12-hour and 24-hour time
description: Convert a time between 12-hour and 24-hour forms and check it.
oneStarDescription: Convert a time and say whether it is morning or evening.
twoStarDescription: Convert it back and show that you return to the start.
threeStarDescription: Write a meeting time in the form the other person uses.

title: Count a collection you own
description: Count a small collection and write the number so you can check it later.
oneStarDescription: Count the items once and write the number and the date.
twoStarDescription: Group them so a second count is easier, and count again.
threeStarDescription: If the two counts differ, look for the missing or extra item and write what you find.

title: Credit an image you may use
description: Use an image only if its terms allow, and write the credit those terms ask for.
oneStarDescription: Find the license or the statement that says you may use the image.
twoStarDescription: Write the credit the terms ask for, next to the image.
threeStarDescription: Set aside one image whose terms you cannot find, and do not use it.

title: Cross to a mark
description: Walk to a marked spot on a cue and stop there.
oneStarDescription: Mark a spot and walk to it from a start line.
twoStarDescription: Start on a cue word and arrive as the line ends.
threeStarDescription: If you arrive early or late, change your start and show the better cross.

title: Darn a small hole
description: Stitch across a small hole in knit fabric so it does not gape.
oneStarDescription: Sew threads across a small hole, anchored in sound fabric.
twoStarDescription: Weave the other direction through those threads.
threeStarDescription: Tug gently and show that the darn stays, or mark it as too weak to wear.

title: Debrief a task
description: After a task, say what worked, what failed, and one change.
oneStarDescription: State what the task produced, in a sentence.
twoStarDescription: Name one thing that failed and one that worked.
threeStarDescription: Choose one change for next time and who will remember it.

title: Decide what not to photograph
description: Read a place's photo rule and leave one thing unphotographed.
oneStarDescription: Find the sign or the notice about photos.
twoStarDescription: Photograph only what it allows, or take no photo.
threeStarDescription: Point to one thing you did not photograph because of the rule or because a person did not agree.

title: Decline a photo of yourself
description: Say no to a photo, or ask where it will go before you agree.
oneStarDescription: Before you agree, ask who will see the photo.
twoStarDescription: Agree, refuse, or agree only without your face, in a clear sentence.
threeStarDescription: If you refused and they ask again, repeat the no once and move away or change the subject.

title: Describe a dance you watched
description: Describe a dance you watched by naming one movement and one change, without claiming you can dance it.
oneStarDescription: Name one movement you saw, in ordinary words.
twoStarDescription: Say what changed when the music or the pattern changed.
threeStarDescription: Say you are not teaching the dance, and do not demonstrate a step you cannot do safely.

title: Describe a quiet moment
description: Describe a moment that is quiet, including the small sounds that remain.
oneStarDescription: Find a quieter spot and say what got softer.
twoStarDescription: Name one sound that is still there.
threeStarDescription: Say whether the spot is quiet enough for the task you had in mind, such as reading aloud.

title: Describe an image aloud
description: Describe an image so a person who cannot see it knows what is there and what you are guessing.
oneStarDescription: Describe the main subject of an image in two sentences a listener can check if they look later.
twoStarDescription: Mark one thing you are inferring, such as a mood or a place, and one thing you can actually see.
threeStarDescription: Answer one question about the image, or say the image does not show it.

title: Design a one-page sign
description: Make a sign with one message that a person can read at a glance.
oneStarDescription: Write the one thing the sign must say, in a few words.
twoStarDescription: Letter it large, with empty space around the words.
threeStarDescription: Show it briefly to someone and ask what it said. Fix it if they miss the message.

title: Divide a length into equal parts
description: Divide a length into equal parts and check by measuring.
oneStarDescription: Say how many equal parts you want.
twoStarDescription: Mark the parts on a strip or a line.
threeStarDescription: Measure the parts and adjust one mark that is off.

title: Draw a diagram of a process you did
description: Draw a process as boxes and arrows, including one decision.
oneStarDescription: Draw the main steps of a process you did, in order.
twoStarDescription: Add one decision with two arrows.
threeStarDescription: Walk the diagram with someone and fix an arrow that points the wrong way.

title: Draw a three-panel comic
description: Draw three panels in which something changes from the first to the third.
oneStarDescription: Write what the first and last panel show before you draw.
twoStarDescription: Draw three panels so a reader can tell the order.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone what changed, and redraw a panel if they cannot tell.

title: Draw the route of a story
description: Draw where a story you heard or read moved, and mark a place you do not know.
oneStarDescription: List the places the story names, in order.
twoStarDescription: Sketch a path that connects the places you can locate.
threeStarDescription: Mark a place you cannot locate, and do not invent a spot for it.

title: End a rehearsal on time
description: End a practice on the agreed time and say what the next practice will start with.
oneStarDescription: Say the end time at the start.
twoStarDescription: Stop at that time, even mid-run if you must.
threeStarDescription: Say the first thing the next practice will do.

title: Estimate a crowd from a sample
description: Estimate how many people are in a space by counting a part, and show the arithmetic.
oneStarDescription: Count the people in one clearly bounded part of the space.
twoStarDescription: Say how many such parts fit in the space, and multiply.
threeStarDescription: Name one way the crowd is uneven, so the estimate could be off.

title: Explain why a joke worked
description: Say why a joke you heard worked, without repeating a joke that targets a person in the room.
oneStarDescription: Point to the moment the meaning turned.
twoStarDescription: Say what the listener had to assume before the turn.
threeStarDescription: If the joke needs a private fact about someone present, do not retell it, and say you are leaving it.

title: Export a file someone can open
description: Save a file in a form another person can open, and check with them.
oneStarDescription: Ask which kind of file they can open.
twoStarDescription: Export or save in that form and send it.
threeStarDescription: Ask them to open it and resend in another form if they cannot.

title: Feel which handle warms
description: Put two spoons in warm water and say which handle warms first.
oneStarDescription: Put a metal spoon and a wooden or plastic spoon in the same warm water.
twoStarDescription: After a short wait, feel the handles and say which is warmer.
threeStarDescription: Say you compared handles, not a rule for every material.

title: File a clipping with a date
description: Save a short clipping with its date and where it came from.
oneStarDescription: Save a clipping or a link you are allowed to keep.
twoStarDescription: Write the date and the publication or the page.
threeStarDescription: Find it again from the date or the topic, and fix the label if you could not.

title: Find a public meeting
description: Find the time and place of a public meeting from an official notice.
oneStarDescription: Find a notice that names a meeting.
twoStarDescription: Write the time and the place, including whether it is online.
threeStarDescription: Check that the date has not passed, or say the notice is old.

title: Find a rhyme
description: Find the rhymes in a short poem and say where the pattern breaks.
oneStarDescription: Mark the line endings that rhyme.
twoStarDescription: Say which lines rhyme with which.
threeStarDescription: Point to a line that does not fit the pattern, or say the pattern holds.

title: Find a step-free way
description: Find a way into a place that does not use a step, using signs you can see.
oneStarDescription: Find the step-free entrance sign, or say you cannot find one from where you are.
twoStarDescription: Follow the signs to the entrance and stop if the route is blocked.
threeStarDescription: Describe the route in two sentences, including where it failed if it did.

title: Find an accessible entrance on a sign
description: Use a sign or a map at a building to find the entrance that avoids steps.
oneStarDescription: Find the access symbol or the words that point to the entrance.
twoStarDescription: Go there, or say the sign runs out.
threeStarDescription: If the entrance is locked or missing, note that and the time.

title: Find the chorus of a song
description: Listen to a song and point to the part that returns.
oneStarDescription: Listen to a song you are allowed to play and note a part that comes back.
twoStarDescription: Play or sing the start of that part when it returns.
threeStarDescription: Say one thing that is different the second time, or that it is the same.

title: Find the plain meaning of an idiom
description: Find what an idiom means in plain words, and the situation it came from if you know it.
oneStarDescription: Look up an idiom and write the plain meaning.
twoStarDescription: Use it in a sentence where it fits, or say the situation is wrong for it.
threeStarDescription: If you tell where the phrase came from, mark that as a story you sourced, or leave it out.

title: Find the poles of a magnet
description: Find which ends of two magnets attract and which resist.
oneStarDescription: Bring two magnets together and show an end that resists.
twoStarDescription: Mark the ends that attract each other and check the mark a second time.
threeStarDescription: Predict whether two marked ends will attract or resist, then test it.

title: Find who made an object
description: Find the maker or the source of an object from a mark, a label, or a catalog.
oneStarDescription: Look for a signature, a label, or a stamp, and write what it says or that there is none.
twoStarDescription: If there is a name or a number, look it up in the place's list or catalog.
threeStarDescription: Write whether you found a person, a workshop, or only a number, and what you still do not know.

title: Find who runs a local service
description: Find the office responsible for a local service, from a page or a sign you can show.
oneStarDescription: Write the service you mean, such as the library or the park.
twoStarDescription: Find a page or a sign that names the office, and save the name.
threeStarDescription: Find one official way to ask a question, or say you could not.

title: Fit a battery the right way
description: Match a battery to the marks in a device and seat the cover.
oneStarDescription: Point to the plus and minus marks in the compartment and on the battery.
twoStarDescription: Insert the battery so the marks agree, and close the cover.
threeStarDescription: Turn the device on, or say it still does not work and you will not force another battery in.

title: Fold a one-page zine
description: Fold one sheet into a small booklet with a cover and an order.
oneStarDescription: Fold one sheet into a booklet and number the pages in reading order.
twoStarDescription: Add a title and one idea that continues across the pages.
threeStarDescription: Give it to someone and ask which page they read after the cover.

title: Fold a paper envelope
description: Fold an envelope that closes and holds a card.
oneStarDescription: Fold a sheet so three sides can hold a card.
twoStarDescription: Tuck or stick the flap so the card stays in when you turn it over.
threeStarDescription: Write a practice address on it, or say you will use a real envelope for the post.

title: Fold a letter and put it in an envelope
description: Fold a letter so it fits an envelope and the greeting is what you see first when it opens.
oneStarDescription: Fold the letter so it fits the envelope without forcing.
twoStarDescription: Fold so the greeting is visible first when the reader opens it.
threeStarDescription: Seal a practice envelope or leave it unsealed for the post, and say which.

title: Follow a cross-reference
description: Follow a see-also reference and say whether it answered your question.
oneStarDescription: Point to a see-also or a footnote marker.
twoStarDescription: Go to the place it names.
threeStarDescription: Say whether the new place answered the question, or that you need another source.

title: Follow a folding diagram
description: Follow a folding diagram one picture at a time and undo a wrong fold.
oneStarDescription: Make the first fold so your paper matches the first picture.
twoStarDescription: Follow the next pictures in order until the object is done or you are stuck.
threeStarDescription: If a fold is wrong, unfold to the last picture that matched, and say which picture.

title: Give a three-stop tour
description: Guide someone through three stops you know, with one true fact at each.
oneStarDescription: Pick three stops and one fact you can point to at each.
twoStarDescription: Take a person to the three stops in order and say the fact at the place.
threeStarDescription: When they ask something you do not know, say so, and do not invent a date or a name.

title: Host one quiet minute
description: Ask a group for one quiet minute and say what it was for.
oneStarDescription: Tell the group why you want one quiet minute.
twoStarDescription: Start it and end it, and stay quiet yourself.
threeStarDescription: Ask if anyone wants to say one thing they noticed, and accept silence.
